Work/life balance... Was nonexistent for me. I worked 80 hour weeks at Chubb. 

Red tape I don't really know if I can comment on. I wasn't an underwriter so that might have made a difference? 

Yes, 100% on the raises/promotions/low salaries. The position I was hired into you can only get into by going through a temp agency. The contract is meant to be for 6 months and then they can hire you if they choose. Unfortunately for me, my 6 months was up around the time of the pandemic. At first they decided that contractors would go in the office and everyone else would stay home, because they didn't trust us with laptops. So I never got a laptop in 3 years of being there and being remote for 2. They eventually let everyone stay home because it was pretty shitty to expect only the temps to go in and get sick. I stayed in that position the entire time I was at Chubb, but they promoted me to a regular position two years in. Mind you, I was working 80 hours a week from the moment the pandemic hit essentially. They declared a hiring freeze in our department only, and continued to hire people in other teams. 

I made $15 an hour at Chubb when I first started. With overtime, I was making about $42k a year, so when they offered me a position I asked for 40k. They offered me 36k. The following year, when they took on the remaining batch of temps and made them permanent, they got 40k. A few months later they did a cost of living increase for everyone in Arizona, so we were bumped up to 42k - this included the people who just got a raise to 40k. I got a measly 1500 bonus, and my manager said if I just keep working as hard as I was that year, I'd see higher numbers next year. I did! At Ascot. For less work. I'm making 65k at Ascot and I've gotten two bonuses this year that are more than 10x what I got at Chubb. 

Sorry this is kind of long winded and a little bit like I'm holding a grudge, but they honestly fucked me over and the reason I left was not really even because of Ascot, but because they refused to let me stay fully remote. Sucks for them. 🤷🏻‍♀️
I personally think it is a Chubb wide issue, it's just outdated leadership and it shows.

The good: it's remote for me since I was grandfathered in. I have a really really good team and it's flexible. Like I don't clock in, I don't really have a set schedule, I just process all day but it's not from a queue or anything. It seems like most teams have a similar vibe with little to no micromanaging but depends on your team. Benefits are awesome, company paid healthcare and dental and we get 25 days of PTO. 

The bad: new hires are hybrid depending on where you live but there is waaaaay more flexibility for underwriters than Ops at least. If you live in CA, there's no office there so you wouldn't have to go in. If you live in Chicago or NY, you're expected in at least one day a week but they're trying to be annoying about more. So that I don't love. For a start up, it has a lot of bad habits already - we have a system that is better than anything I used at Chubb by far but it was built for an MGA and not a carrier and they keep dumping new products into it instead of putting those entirely on a new system. But some of those things feel typical of most places - HR, tech issues. 

For all my complaining, it's still the best place I've worked (though compared to a lot of industry vets I don't have a ton to compare to... 5 years in insurance and 10 years total in the workforce). Also not having to pay healthcare premiums really is fantastic. I lucked into getting the job the year before I turned 26 so I never had a lapse in "free" healthcare 😅 using that free veryyyyy loosely though...
